body: Why can't we just use the range of the `TypeNode` in `return_type`?

I'd say it's a parser bug. Comes from the fact that by default new nodes include the range of the previous token (e.g. `func` triggers `parse_function` and the function node should inlcude the keyword.)

But for type nodes including the triggering token does not make sense, it isn't even the same in all contexts (`->` for functions `:` for variables).

If you want to do it with the type chain, please explain the rational in a comment.

Alrighty, your reasoning makes sense there to me! I think for now to keep minimal changes to the underlying behavior, and because I don't think the type chain approach will cause a major increase in overhead, I'll keep it for now but add an explanation in a comment as you requested. Then, in a separate PR we can fix ranges for TypeNodes and perhaps move this functionality to use those ranges after that.

```suggestion
			push_error(R"(Not all code paths return a value.)", p_function->return_type ? p_function->return_type : p_function);
```

`mark_node_unsafe` is only what marks the safe line feature in the editor. It's not compilation critical in any way. If we push an error, the safe lines are practically irrelevant, so no need to add all this boilerplate.
Thanks for noting how the previous line and column collection code is no longer necessary! It'd totally slipped my mind that with the TypeNode range bug now fixed, we no longer need to do that 😅
Yep, as I was fixing up the changes/commit history, I realized now the overload for `push_error()` was unused, so it's all gone now and the PR can (I think) be just a +2-1 change 🥳

```suggestion
			push_error(R"(Not all code paths return a value.)", p_function->return_type ? static_cast<GDScriptParser::Node *>(p_function->return_type) : static_cast<GDScriptParser::Node *>(p_function);
```

I think we prefer C++ style casts for objects style wise.
